core_obligations: Reduce to a free module (proof line 11788): since a direct summand of a finite free module is a summand of O_U^{direct sum n}, it is enough to treat the case E = O_U^{direct sum n}, the general case following by restriction of the dotted arrow along the inclusion of the summand.

Translate to a lifting problem for sections (proof lines 11789-11790): a morphism O_U^{direct sum n} -> F is the same as a tuple of sections of F, so finding the dotted arrow is equivalent to lifting the images of the basis elements in Gamma(U, F) along the surjection p.

Lift locally (proof lines 11790-11792): by the characterisation of surjective maps of sheaves, a section of G and a preimage under p admit a covering over whose members a lift exists, so the required dotted arrow exists over the members of a covering.
proof_roadmap: Reduce to E free of finite rank.
Read a map out of a finite free module as a tuple of sections.
Use the local characterisation of surjectivity of sheaf maps to lift those sections on a covering.
Conclude the existence of the dotted arrow on the members of a covering.
difficulty_reason: The lemma lifts a map from a direct summand of a finite free module along a surjection of O_U-modules, locally on a covering (statement lines 11771-11785). The proof reduces to the free case (proof lines 11788) and then observes that a map out of a finite free module is a tuple of sections, so the lifting problem becomes the local liftability of sections along a surjection, which is the characterisation of surjective maps of sheaves (proof lines 11789-11792). The non-formal content is the identification of the dotted arrow with lifted sections, which is where finite freeness is used. The claim is H2: a short reduction and one local-liftability statement, with the Xy-pic diagram delivered as written.
